english.title: Aid / abet commission of an act at an election intending to deprive other of vote / gain a vote etc
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) aided, abetted, counselled or procured the commission by **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) of an offence of engaging in the act of

(A)_[applying for a postal or proxy vote as some other person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(B)_[making a false statement in, or in connection with, an application for a postal or proxy vote]_
(C)_[inducing the registration officer or returning officer to send a postal ballot paper or any communication relating to a postal or proxy vote to an address which had not been agreed to by the person entitled to vote]_
(D)_[causing a communication relating to a postal or proxy vote or containing a postal ballot paper not to be delivered to the intended recipient]_

(E)_[at a parliamentary election,]_
(F)_[at a local government election,]_

**(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) intending by so doing to

(G)_[deprive another, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), of an opportunity to vote]_
(H)_[make for yourself or another person a gain of a vote to which you or that other person were not otherwise entitled]_
(I)_[make for yourself or another person a gain of money or property]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 62A(1) and 168(1) of the Representation of the People Act 1983.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 62A of the of the Representation of the People Act 1983 was inserted by section 40 of the Electoral Administration Act 2006.
(ii) Section 62A(5) of the Representation of the People Act 1983 provides that a person who commits this offence is guilty of corrupt practice.
(iii) Section 62A(3) of the Act provides that property includes any description of property.
(iv) Section 62A(4) of the Act provides that a reference to a postal vote or postal ballot paper includes a reference to a proxy postal vote or a proxy postal ballot paper (as the case may be).
(v) The DPP's consent is not required; however, the DPP has certain duties where information is given to the DPP and involvement of CPS/DPP at an early stage would be recommended, see section 181 of the Act.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and/or fine.

Time limit for prosecution:
Complex

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
